_comment: Recipes of the crafting table (see js/business/CraftManager.js). A recipe is an Id, a Grid and a Result. The Grid holds 3 rows of 3 cells, read top to bottom and left to right: a cell is the id of a MINING RESOURCE ('void_dust', 'ultima', ... see settings/mining.json) or null for an empty slot. The shape is matched on its bounding box, so the same recipe works anywhere in the 3x3 table, exactly like a Minecraft recipe: the empty rows and columns around it are ignored.
_results: Result.Type names what the player receives: 'item' adds Result.Quantity of the inventory item Result.Id ('pearl', see EnderPearlManager; 'golden_pickaxe', see GoldenPickaxeManager), 'sparks' credits Result.Quantity Sparks to the balance, and 'resource' adds Result.Quantity of the mining resource Result.Id to the mine. Result.Quantity is a positive integer and defaults to 1.
_statistics: Every committed craft raises stats.itemsCrafted (the trophies of the `crafted` counter). A result of type 'item' or 'resource' counts its Quantity, a batch of 'sparks' counts ONE: Sparks are the currency, not an item. stats.craftedByResult keeps the same count per result id.
_book: The crafting book (the Knowledge Book above the table) lists every recipe with its grid, its name (craft.recipe.<Id>.name) and its description (craft.recipe.<Id>.desc): adding a recipe here is enough for it to be craftable AND listed.

Crafts._comment: The classic Minecraft recipe: eight Void Dust around one Glowstone Dust give one Ender Pearl.
A Golden Pickaxe: two Ultima above two Sculk Dust, joined by a bar of Void Dust. One use buys an extra Mine Pick, see GoldenPickaxeManager.
One Ultima in the center of the table turns into 50 Sparks.
